item.title: Peter Zalmayev: 'Ukraine was showing all sorts of cards that Trump took away and gave to Putin'
item.description: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Peter Zalmayev, Founder and Director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative, LIVE from Kyiv. And he warns, "I'm seeing, I'm smelling a Yalta II. I'm smelling another Munich (1938), where we're seeing appeasement of the aggressor." With this striking historical analogy, Zalmayev captures what he considers the central danger facing Ukraine: the possibility that its sovereignty and security could become bargaining chips in an era Zalmayev describes as great-power "collusion". Zalmayev delivers a forceful critique of the Trump administration's approach to Russia, arguing that Washington is weakening Ukraine's negotiating position while offering Vladimir Putin little incentive to abandon his maximalist demands. His analysis raises questions extending far beyond the immediate prospects for a ceasefire or peace agreement. At stake, he suggests, are the cohesion of the transatlantic alliance, the credibility of Western security commitments and the principle that smaller nations should not have their futures determined by larger powers.

item.title: Concerns mount over artificial intelligence as Silicon Valley sees AI boom
item.description: Tuesday, October 20 saw protests in more than 50 US cities against the rise of artificial intelligence. Demonstrators are calling for a moratorium on AI development, and the sentiment is shared by many: according to a recent study, 71 percent of Americans believe AI will lead to job losses. In the heart of Silicon Valley, record investment is now on a collision course with public fear and uncertainty. FRANCE 24's Pierrick Leurent and Valérie Defert report, with Wassim Cornet.

item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay described the US sanctions imposed on the International Criminal Court (ICC) hours after her award as "a shock" and "unacceptable". item.title: Visual artist Amadeo Carvalho explores Black identity
item.description: From Cape Verde to London and beyond, Amadeo Carvalho is a self-taught, London-based contemporary visual artist putting Black identity, memory and heritage at the heart of his work. Blending painting, poetry and photography, his art explores the stories, silences and connections that shape who we are. This weekend, his powerful collection "Portraits of Absence" arrives at the AKAA Art Fair here in Paris, where it will be exhibited by the curatorial platform Casa Vicência. He spoke to us in Perspective

item.title: Egypt mulls joining Saudi Arabia in war against Houthis
